text:
Hendrix Lapierre is a Penguin now, after Pittsburgh sent Washington a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth for him, and he's the kind of low-cost bet a struggling team should be making. The 22nd pick of the 2020 draft never quite found a full-time role with the Capitals (158 games over parts of several seasons), and he's playing about 12 minutes a night this year.

The production has been tidy for that ice time: seven points in 14 games, a rate above league average for a forward, with two on the power play. Some of that is a shooting percentage (16.7%) that sits above his likely range, so don't expect the scoring pace to hold exactly. What's real is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 22% of his setups crossing the royal road last season, against 7% for a typical forward: the pass that drags a goalie side to side. He's more passer than finisher and rarely shoots. On a team looking at a reset, a 24-year-old centre who makes that pass is worth a longer look.
